STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, medium-large.
b) Reference: the scrambled egg mound is roughly 8 cm across and the meatball-like pieces are about 2.5-3 cm each. The plate spans about 3.3-3.5 meatball lengths... more usefully, the scrambled egg pile spans about 1/3 of the plate width, and the meatballs cluster spans about 1/3 too. Taking the meatball size (~3 cm) and roughly 9 across the plate width gives ~25-27 cm.
Reconciled width: about 24 cm (square), area ≈ 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Scrambled egg: visible footprint about 20% of plate area ≈ 115 cm². Average thickness: a loose layer, about 1.5 cm at the thickest (mound about half peak, so ~1 cm average). Volume ≈ 115 ml. Grams = 115 × 0.8 ≈ 92 g.
- Meatball-like pieces (sausage/meatball style, brown): visible count 6 (one at left, four in the centre cluster, one at lower right, one at bottom). Adding hidden pieces underneath the cluster, roughly 7-8 total. Use 7 × 30 g = 210 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible under the egg; the meatballs sit directly on the plate. No extra items added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Scrambled egg (cooked with some fat): ~150 kcal/100 g.
- Meatballs (pork/beef, cooked): ~250 kcal/100 g.

Totals: egg 92 g → 138 kcal; meatballs 210 g → 525 kcal. Total ≈ 302 g, ≈ 663 kcal.
